Book a Demo experdaAI is a private analytics assistant that turns a plain-language question into a governed, sourced answer from your own databases. The numbers, the chart and the audit trail in one reply; It runs on your premises, inside your network, under each user's existing permissions. Your data is already there. The answers are the bottleneck. Most organisations do not have a data problem. They have a queue: every question that matters has to pass through the two or three people who can write the query, and each round trip costs a day. Self-service BI was supposed to fix this. In practice it moved the bottleneck to dashboard authoring — the question you have today was not anticipated by the dashboard somebody built last quarter. What changes with Experda AI The question is the interface. A regional manager asks in their own words, gets the number and the chart in seconds, and can see exactly which query produced it — without learning SQL and without opening a ticket. Your data never leaves. Experda AI is installed inside your perimeter, on your hardware, against your databases. The model proposes a query; the platform decides whether it may run, under whose permissions, and records the result. Nothing about that decision is delegated to the AI. Follow the data Four zones. The AI provider never talks to your database, and the browser never holds a key. Never give an AI agent a database login of its own. Even a “read-only” agent with an unscoped connection can read every row of every customer, for every user who asks. How Experda AI avoids it The user’s identity and data scope are attached to the request by the platform, in code, before the model is ever called. The model can compose a query; it cannot choose whose data that query runs against, and it cannot widen its own scope by asking. Row-level scope is injected server-side, not passed as a hint to the model A guard rejects INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ALTER outright Result-size and runtime caps stop a runaway query from loading the estate Queries hit curated analytics views, not raw operational tables What an admin can see afterwards Every answer leaves a record: who asked, in which category, which tools ran, how long they took, how many tokens they cost.
